newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs lower on long liquidation and hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: JGBs lower on long liquidation and hedge selling.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was sharply lower in early morning trade on Thursday, retaining weak sentiment from LIFFE overnight, traders said.
The fall on LIFFE triggered long liquidation and hedge selling this morning, said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
"JGBs are looking totally towards the downside now. They are being sold due to weak market sentiment," he said.
The June stood at 122.48 as of 0043 GMT down from the previous day's close of 122.90.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.740 percent as of 0045 GMT, up from the previous day's close of 2.685 percent.
Traders said investors have been sidelined recently, due to fluctuations in the JGB market.
"The fluctuations in the market have been too wild for investors to buy," a trust bank trader said.
Investors are also wary of trading ahead of the release of the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey, the trader said.
The BOJ said on Wednesday that it would release the next tankan survey on June 25.
JGBs may receive some support from short-covering ahead of a shift forward in the benchmark status from the June to the September, the trust bank trader said.
Sentiment is probably too weak, however, for market participants to actively build fresh long positions, he said.
